prompt: What is the nonzero solution to $x^2 - 5x = 0$?
hint: There is no constant term in this equation. Look at what the two terms that remain have in common.

hints.text: There is no constant term in this equation. Look at what the two terms that remain have in common.
Both terms contain $x$, so factor it out to get $x(x - 5) = 0$. Then set each factor equal to zero.
The factors give $x = 0$ and $x = 5$, so the nonzero solution is $5$.

learningObjective: Solve a quadratic with no constant term by factoring out the variable.
explanation: Factor out the common $x$ rather than dividing by it, so no solution is lost: $x(x - 5) = 0$.
A product is zero only when one factor is zero, so either $x = 0$ or $x - 5 = 0$.
The second case gives $x = 5$, so the nonzero solution is $5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Never divide both sides by x
steps: Dividing $x^2 = 5x$ by $x$ gives $x = 5$ — but it silently destroys the solution $x = 0$.
Dividing by a variable is only safe when you know it is not zero, and here it might be.
Move everything to one side and factor instead; you keep every solution that way.
